pack: Witnesses outside the Gospels: the death of Jesus

properties.name: Tacitus — Annals 15.44 (Rome)
properties.found: Roman senator-historian Tacitus (c. 116 CE) reports that "Christus" was executed under Tiberius by the procurator Pontius Pilate, in the context of Nero blaming Christians for the fire of 64 CE.
properties.support: Latin, Annals 15.44 (short key words: 'Christus ... supplicio adfectus erat'). Paraphrase: the man the name comes from, Christus, was put to death under Tiberius by Pontius Pilate.
properties.notes: Native language: Latin. Written at Rome. Hostile witness, calls the movement a "superstition".
properties.caveat: Overwhelmingly accepted as authentic; debate is over his source (Roman records vs. Christian hearsay) and the "procurator" title (Pilate was technically prefect).
properties.author: Publius Cornelius Tacitus
caveats: Text is accepted as genuine by nearly all scholars.
Minor debate: where Tacitus got his facts (Roman files or what Christians said).
He calls Pilate 'procurator'; in Jesus' time the title was 'prefect' (Pilate inscription, Caesarea).
A small debate exists over whether the oldest manuscript first read 'Chrestianos'; it does not change the point.

properties.name: Josephus — Antiquities 18.63-64 & 20.200 (Rome)
properties.found: Jewish historian Flavius Josephus (c. 93-94 CE) mentions Jesus, "a wise man", condemned to the cross by Pilate (18.63-64, the Testimonium Flavianum), and James "the brother of Jesus who was called Christ" (20.200).
properties.support: Greek. 20.200 (short): 'the brother of Jesus who was called Christ, named James.' 18.64 paraphrase: after leading men accused him, Pilate sentenced him to the cross.
properties.notes: Native language: Greek (Josephus was a Judean writing in Rome under Flavian patronage). An Arabic paraphrase preserved by Agapius of Hierapolis (10th c.) gives a more neutral wording.
properties.caveat: Most scholars hold 18.63-64 has a genuine core with later Christian interpolations ("he was the Christ"); 20.200 is widely accepted as authentic.
properties.author: Flavius Josephus
caveats: Most scholars think 18.63-64 has a real core that Christian copyists later added to (lines like 'he was the Christ').
A few scholars think the whole passage was added; a few think all of it is genuine.
20.200 about James is accepted by most scholars.

properties.name: Mara bar Serapion — Letter to his son (Samosata)
properties.found: A Syriac letter (after 73 CE?) by a Stoic prisoner from Samosata asks what the Jews gained by killing their "wise king", alongside Socrates and Pythagoras.
properties.support: Syriac letter, British Library Add. MS 14658. Paraphrase: the Jews gained nothing by executing their wise king, since their kingdom was taken away.
properties.notes: Native language: Syriac. Author location: Samosata (Commagene, now under Atatürk Dam lake, Turkey). Does not name Jesus.
properties.caveat: Date disputed (73 CE to 3rd c.); identification of the "wise king" with Jesus is probable but not certain.
properties.author: Mara bar Serapion
properties.written_at: Unknown; author from Samosata (letter possibly written in Roman captivity)
properties.date_range: after 73 CE (some argue 2nd-3rd c.); manuscript 6th-7th c.
caveats: The letter never names Jesus; 'wise king' is most likely Jesus but that is a guess.
Date is uncertain.
Only one manuscript (British Library Add. MS 14658).

properties.name: Thallus via Julius Africanus (Rome / Emmaus-Nicopolis)
properties.found: Julius Africanus (c. 221 CE), writing at Emmaus-Nicopolis, says Thallus explained the darkness at the crucifixion as a solar eclipse — which Africanus rejects since Passover falls at full moon.
properties.support: Greek fragment preserved in George Syncellus. Paraphrase: Thallus calls this darkness an eclipse of the sun, unreasonably, it seems to me.
properties.notes: Thallus himself wrote in Greek (mid-1st c.? at Rome); his work is lost. Pin is at Emmaus-Nicopolis where Africanus lived.
properties.caveat: Thallus' date and whether he actually mentioned Jesus are disputed; known only third-hand.
properties.author: Thallus (via Sextus Julius Africanus)
properties.written_at: Thallus: unknown (possibly Rome); Africanus: Emmaus-Nicopolis region
properties.date_range: Thallus: 1st-2nd c. CE (disputed); Africanus Chronographiai c. 221 CE; quoted by Syncellus c. 800 CE
caveats: Thallus' own book is lost; we only have a later writer quoting another writer.
It is not certain Thallus named Jesus; he may only have described a darkness or eclipse.
His date is uncertain.

properties.name: Phlegon of Tralles — Olympiads (Tralles)
properties.found: Phlegon, freedman of Hadrian, recorded a great eclipse and earthquake in Olympiad 202 (c. 32-33 CE); Origen and Africanus link it to the crucifixion darkness.
properties.support: Greek fragment via Eusebius/Africanus/Origen (Contra Celsum 2.33, 2.59). Paraphrase: in the 4th year of the 202nd Olympiad there was a great eclipse, night at the sixth hour, and an earthquake in Bithynia.
properties.notes: Native language: Greek. Author location: Tralles (Aydın, Turkey), working at Rome.
properties.caveat: Phlegon did not mention Jesus himself in surviving fragments; the eclipse link is a Christian inference, and a real solar eclipse of 29 CE (Nov 24) may be meant.
properties.author: Phlegon of Tralles
properties.date_range: Olympiads written c. 137-140s CE; eclipse dated Olympiad 202.4 = 32/33 CE
caveats: Phlegon's surviving words do not mention Jesus; Christian writers made the link.
Known only through later quotes (Africanus, Origen, Eusebius), and the year wording differs between quotes.
A real solar eclipse on 24 Nov 29 CE fits his report better than a Passover darkness.

properties.name: Pliny the Younger — Letter 10.96 (Amastris / Bithynia)
properties.found: Governor Pliny (c. 112 CE) writes to Trajan about Christians who sing hymns "to Christ as to a god" and asks how to try them.
properties.support: Latin: "carmenque Christo quasi deo dicere secum invicem." Paraphrase: they sang alternately a hymn to Christ as to a god.
properties.notes: Native language: Latin. Written while governor of Bithynia-Pontus (letters 10.96-98 sent from the province; Amastris/Nicomedia region).
properties.caveat: Authentic; does not mention the crucifixion directly — evidences early worship of Christ.
properties.author: Gaius Plinius Caecilius Secundus
properties.solidity: weak (on the death); text itself strong
caveats: The letter is genuine.
It does not mention Jesus' death; it shows Christians worshiped Christ by about 110 CE.
Pin city is approximate.

properties.name: Suetonius — Claudius 25.4 / Nero 16.2 (Rome)
properties.found: Suetonius (c. 121 CE) reports Claudius expelled Jews from Rome who rioted "impulsore Chresto", and that Nero punished Christians.
properties.support: Latin: "Iudaeos impulsore Chresto assidue tumultuantis Roma expulit." Paraphrase: he expelled the Jews who were constantly rioting at the instigation of Chrestus.
properties.notes: Native language: Latin. Written at Rome (imperial secretary under Hadrian).
properties.caveat: "Chrestus" is likely a garbled Christus, but could be an unrelated person; says nothing about the death itself.
properties.author: Gaius Suetonius Tranquillus
properties.date_range: Lives of the Caesars c. 121 CE
caveats: 'Chrestus' may mean Christ, or a different person with a common slave name.
Says nothing about Jesus' death.
Nero 16.2 only says Christians were punished.

properties.name: Lucian of Samosata — Death of Peregrinus 11, 13 (Athens)
properties.found: Satirist Lucian (c. 165 CE) mocks Christians who worship "that crucified sophist" executed in Palestine for introducing a new cult.
properties.support: Greek, ch. 11: "τὸν ἄνθρωπον τὸν ἐν τῇ Παλαιστίνῃ ἀνασκολοπισθέντα" — the man who was crucified (literally 'impaled/fixed on a stake') in Palestine. Ch. 13: "τὸν δὲ ἀνεσκολοπισμένον ἐκεῖνον σοφιστὴν αὐτὸν προσκυνῶσιν" — they worship that crucified sophist himself. 'Sophist' is a mocking word here (a clever teacher/charlatan).
properties.notes: Native language: Greek. Lucian was from Samosata but wrote Peregrinus while living in Athens.
properties.caveat: Authentic but late and satirical; reflects 2nd-c. public knowledge rather than independent records.
properties.author: Lucian of Samosata
caveats: Genuine text, but it is satire meant to mock.
It is late and repeats common knowledge, not an independent record.
Supports that people widely knew Jesus was crucified in Palestine.

properties.name: Celsus — The True Word (preserved by Origen at Caesarea)
properties.found: Pagan philosopher Celsus (c. 175-180 CE) attacked Christianity; preserved fragments accept that Jesus was executed but ridicule the resurrection.
properties.support: Greek fragments quoted in Origen, Contra Celsum (e.g. 2.9, 2.55). Paraphrase: a man punished and crucified cannot have been God.
properties.notes: Native language: Greek. Place of writing unknown (Rome or Alexandria proposed) — pin tentative at Alexandria where Origen worked.
properties.caveat: Known only through Origen's rebuttal; authorship location uncertain.
properties.author: Celsus
properties.written_at: Celsus: unknown (Rome or Alexandria suggested); Origen wrote Contra Celsum at Caesarea Maritima
properties.date_range: Celsus c. 175-180 CE; Origen c. 248 CE
caveats: We only have Celsus through quotes in his opponent Origen.
Shows that a hostile writer accepted the crucifixion as fact.
Place of writing unknown; pin moved to Caesarea Maritima where Origen preserved the text.

properties.name: Babylonian Talmud Sanhedrin 43a (Sura / Pumbedita)
properties.found: A baraita says "on the eve of Passover they hanged Yeshu" after a herald announced charges of sorcery and leading Israel astray.
properties.support: Hebrew (baraita): "בערב הפסח תלאוהו לישו" — on the eve of Passover they hanged Yeshu; some manuscripts add הנוצרי ('the Notzri', often read 'the Nazarene'). תלאוהו (tela'uhu) = 'they hanged him'. (Uncensored manuscripts, e.g. Munich Cod. Hebr. 95; manuscripts differ in wording.)
properties.notes: Native language: Hebrew/Jewish Babylonian Aramaic. Compiled in the Babylonian academies (Sura / Pumbedita, Iraq), 3rd-6th c. Pin approximate at Sura.
properties.caveat: Late and polemical; scholars debate whether "Yeshu" here is Jesus of Nazareth and whether it preserves any independent tradition. Censored from many printed editions.
properties.author: Babylonian Talmud (anonymous baraita)
properties.date_range: Edited c. 500-600 CE; the passage claims earlier tradition
caveats: Written centuries later and hostile.
Scholars disagree whether this 'Yeshu' is Jesus of Nazareth.
It says 'hanged' (likely meaning executed and hung up) and gives no Roman role.
Removed from many printed editions by censors; found in older manuscripts.

properties.name: Agapius of Hierapolis — Kitab al-Unwan (Manbij)
properties.found: 10th-c. Arabic world chronicle quoting a version of Josephus' passage on Jesus: Pilate condemned him to be crucified; his disciples reported he appeared alive after three days.
properties.support: Arabic (Vasiliev, Patrologia Orientalis 7; Pines 1971): "فحكم عليه بيلاطس بالصلب والموت" — Pilate condemned him to be crucified and to die. The passage then hedges: his disciples 'reported that he had appeared to them three days after his crucifixion and that he was alive; accordingly he was perhaps the Messiah'. It is reported belief, not the chronicler's own claim.
properties.notes: Native language: Arabic. Author bishop of Hierapolis/Mabbug (Manbij, Syria).
properties.caveat: Medieval; value lies in possibly preserving a less-interpolated Testimonium. Debated (Pines vs. later critics).
properties.author: Agapius (Mahbub) of Hierapolis
properties.solidity: moderate (as a witness to the Josephus text); weak as an independent source
caveats: Very late; it is a retelling, not an exact copy.
Some scholars think it shows an earlier, less-edited Josephus; others think it comes from Christian sources.
Arabic wording checked against Pines 1971 (language check 2026-10-10).

properties.name: Qur'an 4:157 (Medina)
properties.found: The Qur'an (7th c.) addresses the crucifixion, denying that Jesus was killed or crucified — "it was made to appear so to them".
properties.support: Arabic: "وَمَا قَتَلُوهُ وَمَا صَلَبُوهُ وَلَٰكِن شُبِّهَ لَهُمْ" — they did not kill him, nor did they crucify him, but it was made to appear so to them (shubbiha lahum). Muslim interpreters differ on what this means (a look-alike substitute, or only the appearance of a death); it is a theological statement, not a historical record of the death.
properties.notes: Native language: Arabic. Surah 4 is a Medinan surah. Included as a world-tradition reference, not an independent historical witness.
properties.caveat: Not a historical record of the event; included because it shows how the death was discussed in Arabia. Present in counterpoint to the other witnesses.
properties.author: Qur'an (Medinan surah)
caveats: This is scripture, not a history record.
It denies the death happened, the opposite of the other pins.
Shown only so readers see how the event was discussed in Arabia.
